reason: The passage depicts a strongly affirmed hierarchical structure: God stands as supreme authority, commanding Abram ('lech-lecha,' go); Abram demonstrates obedience ('vayeilech Abraham ka'asher dibber elayv Adonai,' and Abram went as the Lord spoke to him), establishing himself as head of his household; and his family and servants follow under his authority. The covenant relationship itself is predicated on this hierarchical framework—God makes binding promises to Abram based on his position of authority. There is no suggestion that hierarchy is unimportant or discouraged; rather, the text affirms obedience to established authority as normative and proper.
